_README: Single source of the book's structure; the build is driven ENTIRELY by this file. Chapter ids start with 'ch'. A chapter counts as translated once out/<id>_reading.md exists. Cite the PRINTED FOLIO in notes, never the PDF page. THIS BOOK: Japanese, vertical (top-to-bottom, right-to-left), with heavy furigana (rubi). Source-title/author fields are named *_zh for historical reasons but hold the Japanese source text; source_script='ja' tags them.

description: The closing arc of Murayama Tomoyoshi's celebrated ninja saga. In the wake of Oda Nobunaga's death, the legendary thief and shinobi Ishikawa Goemon is pulled from a quiet peasant life in Saiga into a war of vengeance against Toyotomi Hideyoshi, whose brutal campaigns have destroyed everyone Goemon loved. It is a road that ends, as history records, at the cauldron. A vivid Sengoku-era historical novel by one of modern Japan's major playwright-novelists.

translator_note: This is an English translation of Shinobi no mono (忍びの者), subtitle Goemon kamairi (五右衛門釜煎り), by Tomoyoshi Murayama (村山知義, 1901–1977), from an image-only scan of the 1987 Kobunsha bunko edition with no digital text layer.

The source is set vertically, right to left, and is printed with dense furigana (small kana glosses beside the kanji giving their reading). The text was recovered by optical character recognition tuned for vertical Japanese, with every proper name, number, and uncertain reading verified by eye against magnified crops of the scan before translation.

The novel is a work of historical fiction set in the late sixteenth century, in the years around the fall of Oda Nobunaga and the rise of Toyotomi Hideyoshi. Its hero, Ishikawa Goemon, is the semi-legendary outlaw whose death by boiling is part of Japanese popular memory; Murayama, a lifelong man of the political left, reads the ninja and the peasant world through that lens. Footnotes supply the historical figures, places, institutions, and customs a reader outside Japan would miss, and flag where the author writes as an interested witness of his own century.
Damaged, missing, or genuinely ambiguous passages are handled honestly in the notes rather than smoothed over; no bridging text is ever invented.
source_note: Image-only PDF scan, 537 pages, no text layer (PDF creator '1lib.sk'; the PDF's own bookmarks are just sequential page stubs and the labels 封面/版权/封底 were added by the scanner, not the book). Vertical Japanese, right-to-left, heavy furigana. Folio printed at the top OUTER corner; no running head or foot down the margins. Colour cover on PDF p1; publisher back-cover blurb on p537.
_offset_note: PDF-to-printed offset is a CONSTANT +2 across the whole book (printed = pdf - 2): this is a text-only novel with no unpaginated plates, verified at every chapter opener and at the afterword. pdf_page below is the chapter DIVIDER page (= printed_page + 2).
_end_note: The novel body (8 chapters) ends at printed 528 (PDF 530). The afterword 解説 by Musashino Jiro runs printed 529-534 (PDF 531-536) and is NOT part of the chapter structure. DECIDED: it will be translated as clearly-attributed back matter in the final batch (B09).
toc_flags_resolved: Printed TOC (PDF p5) lists 8 chapters + 解説; verified against the scan. No internal numbered sections within chapters (continuous prose with scene breaks). Offset +2 confirmed at all eight openers.
_structure_note: 8 chapters, no sections. Reading markdown uses '## ' for the chapter; scene breaks inside a chapter are '***' (asterism), not structural sections.
